question.problem: Find the disjoint union of the sets ${A}_{1}=\{1,3,5\}$ and ${A}_{2}=\{5,10,15\}.$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sets are overlapping since

$$
\{1,3,5\}\cap \{5,10,15\}=\{5\}\ne ∅.
$$

So, for each of our sets, we form the associated set, where each element is tagged with the corresponding index, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {A}_{1} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{1}^{∗}=\{(1,1),(3,1),(5,1)\} \\  & {A}_{2} &  & \,\to \, &  & {A}_{2}^{∗}=\{(5,2),(10,2),(15,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the disjoint union of our sets is simply the union of the associated tagged sets:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1}⊔{A}_{2} & =\{1,3,5\}⊔\{5,10,15\} \\  & ={A}_{1}^{∗}\cup {A}_{2}^{∗} \\  & =\{(1,1),(3,1),(5,1)\}\cup \{(5,2),(10,2),(15,2)\} \\  & =\{(1,1),(3,1),(5,1),(5,2),(10,2),(15,2)\}\end{aligned}
$$
